description.narrative:
Stakeholders effects Improved access to finance for MSMEs including underserved segments.
The MSME financing gap in the country is estimated at US$6.9 billion, representing 16 percent of GDP. The Project is expected to support access to finance for MSMEs including women-owned and youth-led enterprises and rural MSMEs that still face access to finance binding constraints.
Contribution to Market Creation Competitiveness
ENDA has been investing heavily in digital infrastructure to reduce their operational costs and improving the offering for their clients. ENDA has also digitized its loan origination system and processes by undertaking tasks like digital KYC, automated verification of data and decentralization of decision making. As a market leader ENDA can improve the competitiveness of the market by demonstrating such digital capabilities that can be emulated by competitors, thereby improving the overall standards and competitiveness of the microfinance market in Tunisia.

The proposed investment consists of a five-year senior unsecured Tunisian dinars loan of up to EUR100 million equivalent in local currency (LCY) to ENDA Tamweel (the Borrower or The MFI), split as follows: (i) up to EUR40 million on IFC own account, and (ii) up to EUR60 million syndicated parallel loan(s). The proceeds of the IFC loans (deliverable and non-deliverable loans) will be used to on-lend to MSMEs in Tunisia to help preserve and sustain low-income jobs. The team expects the following breakdown of the proceeds facility: 50% to women and women-owned businesses, 30% to the youth and young entrepreneurs, and 50% in rural areas (the Project).
